---
title: "apply() on a data.frame turns everything into text"
ref: DF-02
categories: [Data frames and lists]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "`FALSE TRUE`: only the price of 12 is above 9"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
sales <- data.frame(
  product = c("A", "B"),
  price = c(5, 12),
  quantity = c(10, 3)
)
apply(sales, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(row) {
  row[["price"]]
})
apply(sales, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(row) {
  row[["price"]] > 9
})
apply(sales, MARGIN = 1, FUN = function(row) {
  row[["price"]] * row[["quantity"]]
})
```
:::

## Why

`apply()` works on a matrix. So it starts by converting the data.frame with `as.matrix()`, and a matrix holds a single type. Since the `product` column is text, everything becomes text, numbers included, and they are even padded with spaces to the same width: `" 5"` and `"12"`.

The comparison `" 5" > 9` is then made between strings, in alphabetical order, and `"12"` comes before `"9"`. The result is wrong without any warning. Only the multiplication ends in an error.

## The remedy

Work column by column, which is what R does natively, rather than row by row.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
sales$price > 9
sales$price * sales$quantity
```
:::
